data.expected_signal: Control (K multiple of group_size) near-zero error; K=48/gs=32 large error and g_idx missing group 1.

evidence.summary: Control K=64,gs=32 (exact multiple) matches an explicit unpack+dequant reference to max_abs=2.86e-6 (rel 1.9e-7), showing the reference and packing conventions agree with the kernel. For K=48,gs=32 (ceil=2 groups) max_abs=10.90 vs ref_absmax=13.56 (rel 0.803), and for K=96,gs=64 max_abs=9.75 vs 14.57 (rel 0.669). The wrapper's g_idx for K=48,gs=32 has unique values [0] whereas the contract's group_of(k)=k//group_size gives [0,1]: the trailing partial group is collapsed onto the last full group's scale/zero row, so its supplied scales/zeros row is never used.

rationale: kernel.py lines 69-73 use floor division and clamp, while the contract states scales/zeros have ceil(K/group_size) rows and every column must use the group it actually belongs to.

scope_evidence.summary: "every column must be dequantized with the scale and zero-point of the group it actually belongs to, for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size ... scales and zeros are supplied with ceil(K / group_size) rows accordingly."
num_groups = K // group_size; g_idx = clamp(arange(K)//group_size, max=num_groups-1) collapses the trailing partial group into the last full group.

scope_rationale: The contract explicitly names the non-multiple-K case as required behaviour ("for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size"), so a representative K such as 48 with group_size 32 is inside the declared input domain.
statement: For K not an exact multiple of group_size, gptq_matmul assigns the trailing (partial-group) columns to the previous full group's scale/zero row instead of their own final group row, because it uses num_groups = K // group_size and clamps g_idx to num_groups-1; this yields C values differing from the contract's C = A @ dequant(B) with group_of(k) = k // group_size.
